To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social exchange perceptions partially mediate the relationships between P.I.E.D. and affective organizational commitment/job satisfaction whereas economic exchange perceptions fully mediate them.

perceived investment in employee training (PIED) positively affects employees' attitudes (affective commitment and job satisfaction) through the mediating roles both of social exchange and of economic exchange.

social exchange perceptions fully mediated the relationship between P.I.E.D and job satisfaction, whereas social and economic exchange partially mediated the relationship between PIED and affective commitment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mediating role of two different types of exchange in linking PIED with employees' attitudinally positive outcomes.
the question of why employees are committed to and satisfied with an organization that provides them with training and how social exchange theory can explain this phenomenon.
the process of how employees perceive the organization's training investment as a signal for social or economic exchange.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the more employees perceive that they are receiving a social return from the employer's investment in training (i.e. training investment is perceived as the employer's part of social exchange) the more they will feel committed and satisfied.
PIED is positively related to affective organizational commitment/job satisfaction via social exchange perceptions, but negatively related via economic exchange perceptions.
social exchange perceptions are more likely to be perceived as the organization's side of the exchange, while economic exchange perceptions are more perceived as the employee's side.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social exchange perspective is a useful framework for explaining how organizational training investment influences employees' attitudes.
the more employees perceive the employer's investment in their development as a sign of social exchange, the more positive the employee outcomes will be.

employees' perceptions of social exchange mediate the positive effect of PIED on employees' affective organizational commitment, whereas employees' perceptions of economic exchange mediate the negative effect of PIED.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employers should be aware that employees are likely to perceive training investment as an employer's investment in social exchange, rather than economic exchange.
employers need to be aware of how they invest in employee development and the perceptions employees have about this investment, in order to achieve expected outcomes.
the positive effects of PIED on employees' attitudes are not guaranteed.
